podcast.title: Early Two-Piece Band (1992)
podcast.body: The Inbreds, from Kingston, Ontario, emerged around 1992 as one of the early two-piece rock bands. Their appearance preceded the widespread trend of rock duos in the 2000s. "A band from Kingston, Ontario called The Inbreds, showed up starting about, I think it was 1992."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 6: (50-41)

podcast.title: Founder of The Enclave and Todd Sullivan's Mentor
podcast.body: Tom Zutat founded The Enclave, a short-lived boutique record label with significant funding, and was the mentor to Todd Sullivan, who signed Sloan to Geffen. Zutat's ambition was to make Sloan a major hit to prove Geffen wrong, but The Enclave ceased operations within six months. "It was Tom Zutat, the guy who was the mentor of Todd Sullivan, who was signed to Geffen originally."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Sloan In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.title: Jay Ferguson's Hiatus Project
podcast.body: During Sloan's temporary hiatus after "Twice Removed," Jay Ferguson co-managed The In-Breds while also working at Murder Records, demonstrating his continued involvement in the music scene. "Jay spent some time working at Murder Records and co-managed the in-breds."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Sloan In Their Own Words: Part 1

xref.title: Early Two-Piece Band (Mid-1990s)
xref.body: Chicago's Local H appeared a few years after The Inbreds, in the mid-1990s, as another early example of a two-piece rock band. At this time, rock duos were still considered a rarity. "The next one I remember is Chicago's local H, a few years later."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
